categories.name: Nature & Bioacoustics
categories.blurb: Identify plants, birds, animals, and bats from photos or sound.

models.name: BirdNET V2.4
models.license_note: Weights are non-commercial. Education and research count as non-commercial.
models.node_note: No official SDK. Wrap the TFLite model with tfjs-node or convert to ONNX.
models.summary: 6,000+ bird species from audio, worldwide. The standard for on-device bird sound ID — runs on a Raspberry Pi, even a Pi Zero 2 W. 6,522 classes, 0.826 GFLOPs per inference. Ready-made deployments: BirdNET-Pi, BirdNET-Go.

models.name: Google Perch
models.node_note: Community TFLite/ONNX port; run with onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: ~15,000 bird species globally, higher accuracy than BirdNET, Apache-2.0 weights. Outputs 1280-d embeddings you can few-shot match against a handful of labeled clips to build custom classifiers.

models.name: iNaturalist Vision Small
models.node_note: Run the TFLite via tfjs-node or convert to ONNX.
models.summary: iNaturalist's published on-device classifier: ~500 taxa fully offline, plus a 0.7 MB geolocation model that down-ranks species unlikely at your GPS point. Same model family that powers the Seek app. The full 72,000-taxon production model stays private.

models.name: MegaDetector V6
models.task: Detect animals, people, vehicles in camera photos
models.license_note: License varies by variant: MDV6-mit-yolov9-c is MIT; others are Apache-2.0 or AGPL-3.0. Check the Model Zoo.
models.node_note: Python API today; ONNX exports make onnxruntime-node viable.
models.summary: Microsoft AI for Good's camera-trap detector: bounding boxes for 'is something here', not species names. Compact variant is ~2% of V5's size, CPU-friendly, runs on solar field units. Pair with a classifier: detect, crop, classify.

models.name: BatDetect2
models.license_note: Free for non-commercial research; check the repo.
models.node_note: Python only; ONNX conversion needed for Node use.
models.summary: Bat echolocation call detection and species classification for European species. Audio in, annotated call spans plus species out.

models.name: Pl@ntNet-300K
models.node_note: Train in Python, export ONNX, serve with onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: Research-grade plant photo dataset plus PyTorch training code (NeurIPS 2021). Deliberately long-tailed and label-ambiguous, so models trained on it resemble real-world conditions.

categories.name: Speech: STT & TTS
categories.blurb: Transcribe speech to text and synthesize text to speech, fully offline.

models.name: Whisper.cpp
models.node_note: npm wrappers: nodejs-whisper, smart-whisper; or spawn the CLI.
models.summary: C/C++ port of OpenAI Whisper with word timestamps. Tiny/base/small tiers (39M-244M params) run real-time on phones and Pis; quantized ggml files shrink further.

models.name: sherpa-onnx
models.task: STT + TTS + VAD + diarization + denoising, one toolkit
models.node_note: npm i sherpa-onnx-node — official Node addon covering every task.
models.summary: The swiss-army knife of offline speech: streaming and offline STT (Whisper, Moonshine, SenseVoice, Zipformer, Paraformer), TTS (VITS, Kokoro, Matcha), speaker ID, diarization, VAD, keyword spotting, audio tagging, speech denoising, and two-speaker separation — all via ONNX Runtime on x86/ARM/Pi/NPU.

models.name: Moonshine
models.license_note: Some legacy non-English non-streaming models stay under the non-commercial Moonshine Community License.
models.node_note: Available as a sherpa-onnx backend.
models.summary: Edge-first STT from Useful Sensors. Variable-length windows instead of Whisper's fixed 30-second chunks, so short utterances transcribe several times faster. Tiny is 27M params — microcontroller and browser class.

models.name: SenseVoice Small
models.task: STT + emotion recognition + audio events in one pass
models.license_note: FunASR Model License v1.1 permits commercial use with attribution.
models.node_note: Available as a sherpa-onnx backend.
models.summary: Alibaba's multi-task STT: transcription plus emotion recognition plus audio event detection (laughter, music, applause) in a single pass. Mandarin, Cantonese, English, Japanese, Korean. Very fast for its capability.

models.name: Vosk
models.node_note: Official vosk npm binding.
models.summary: Long-established streaming offline STT that runs on Raspberry Pi and Android with ~50 MB per-language models. Stable, boring in the best way.

models.name: Kokoro
models.task: Text to speech, frontier quality at 82M params
models.node_note: npm i kokoro-js — runs in Node and browser WASM.
models.summary: Frontier TTS at 82M params — best quality-per-size available, won an OpenAI TTS arena against much larger models. kokoro-js runs it in the browser (WASM) and Node.

models.name: Piper
models.task: Fast local TTS, many voices and languages
models.license_note: Original rhasspy/piper is MIT but archived; active development is OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl under GPL-3.0. Each voice carries its own terms — check its MODEL_CARD.
models.node_note: VITS/Piper voices work via sherpa-onnx-node, or spawn the binary.
models.summary: One small ONNX model per voice, dozens of languages, real-time on a Raspberry Pi 4. Powers Home Assistant's voice pipeline and the NVDA screen reader.

models.name: MeloTTS
models.node_note: Python-first; ONNX exports exist for onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: High-quality multilingual TTS (English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese, Korean) by MyShell, CPU-realtime capable. Bigger than Kokoro but strong multilingual coverage.

models.name: Echogarden
models.task: Speech toolset: STT, TTS, alignment, translation, separation
models.license_note: Mixed licensing — check which components you use.
models.node_note: npm i echogarden — pure TypeScript.
models.summary: A speech toolset in pure TypeScript: STT (whisper.cpp-backed), TTS, forced alignment, speech translation, language detection, and source separation with a friendly API.

categories.name: Speech: Understanding & Cleanup
categories.blurb: Who spoke, when, and how cleanly — VAD, diarization, denoising, wake words.

models.name: Silero VAD
models.node_note: @ricky0123/vad-node, or raw ONNX via onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: The standard 'is someone speaking' gate before STT. ~1 MB ONNX, 30 ms chunks, 16k/8k sample rates, extremely fast on CPU. Used by everyone.

models.name: pyannote.audio
models.size: Segmentation models are small; pipeline varies
models.license_note: Segmentation models are gated on Hugging Face — accept terms per model card.
models.node_note: Python-first; community ONNX exports exist for onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: The research standard for speaker diarization: who spoke when, overlapped speech detection, and speaker embeddings.

models.name: DeepFilterNet
models.license_note: Free for most uses; commercial terms apply at scale. Verify the repo before shipping.
models.node_note: Similar models (GTCRN, DPDFNet) ship in sherpa-onnx-node's denoiser.
models.summary: Real-time speech denoising (DeepFilterNet3) with a tiny footprint at 48 kHz.

models.name: RNNoise
models.node_note: C library; community WASM builds exist, or shell out.
models.summary: The classic recurrent-network noise suppressor — battle-tested (Firefox shipped it in WebRTC for years) and runs anywhere, including embedded.

models.name: openWakeWord
models.node_note: Python-first; ONNX models port to onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: Wake-word detection ('Hey Jarvis'-style) on-device, with pre-trained models and a training pipeline for custom phrases.

models.name: 3D-Speaker
models.node_note: Python-first; ONNX exports for onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: ModelScope's speaker verification/identification toolkit: embeddings, verification, cross-modal (audio-video) options.

categories.name: Audio: Source Separation & Stems
categories.blurb: Split a mixed track into isolated stems — vocals, drums, bass, other.

models.name: Demucs
models.node_note: The demucs npm package is a JS/ONNX port of Meta's MIT-licensed Demucs.
models.summary: Meta's hybrid-transformer stem separator (vocals/drums/bass/other, or 6-stem splits). The quality leader for music demixing. A JavaScript+ONNX port exists on npm.

models.name: Spleeter
models.task: Music stem separation, fast and light
models.node_note: Python/TF-first; SavedModel to ONNX conversion is straightforward, or spawn the CLI.
models.summary: Deezer's stem separator with 2/4/5-stem models. Older than Demucs and lower quality, but very light and long-proven.

models.name: Open-Unmix
models.node_note: umx.js demo runs the model in-browser via ONNX with quantization.
models.summary: SIGSEP's research reference for music source separation — the basis of much academic work, with a browser demo (umx.js) proving the ONNX path.

categories.name: Audio: Music Transcription & Notation
categories.blurb: Audio to MIDI and notation — a thin but capable lane.

models.name: Basic Pitch
models.node_note: npm i @spotify/basic-pitch — official JS package.
models.summary: Spotify's polyphonic audio-to-MIDI converter: pitch bend, note onsets, works on any instrument including voice and birdsong. Ships TFLite/ONNX/CoreML exports — genuinely on-device.

models.name: MT3
models.node_note: Python/JAX-first; no JS port; ONNX export would be a project.
models.summary: Google's multi-task multitrack transcription: multiple instruments simultaneously into MIDI with a single T5-style model — piano, drums, guitar, full ensembles.

models.name: ChromaPrint
models.node_note: C library; WASM builds exist, or shell out to fpcalc.
models.summary: The AcoustID backend: identify what recording this is by fingerprint matching — Shazam-like ID for your own library, offline on the matching side.

categories.name: Audio: Music & Sound Tagging
categories.blurb: What am I hearing — genre, instruments, mood, or any of 521 sounds.

models.name: YAMNet
models.node_note: TF.js ports run in Node and browser.
models.summary: MobileNetV1-based sound classifier, 0.92M params, 16 kHz mono in, frame-level scores out, real-time on phones. The standard transfer-learning base for custom audio classifiers.

models.name: musicnn
models.task: Music tags: genre, instruments, mood, tempo
models.node_note: Python-first; small CNNs port to ONNX easily.
models.summary: Pre-trained music audio taggers trained on MagnaTagATune and the Million Song Dataset. Ask 'what's in this track' and get tags like guitar, techno, ambient, fast.

models.name: Essentia
models.task: Full audio analysis toolbox (key, chords, BPM, loudness, descriptors)
models.license_note: AGPL matters for commercial use — see their docs for dynamic-linking discussion.
models.node_note: npm i essentia.js — WASM builds.
models.summary: MTG's C++ audio and music analysis toolbox: tonal, rhythm, loudness, spectral descriptors plus ML model inference. The 'everything else in audio analysis' entry.

models.name: Detoxify
models.node_note: Python-first; transformers.js can load the same weights.
models.summary: Toxicity classification for comments and moderation, trained on all three Jigsaw Toxic Comment challenges. Small BERT-class models.

categories.name: Image Editing & Restoration
categories.blurb: Remove backgrounds, erase objects, add objects realistically, restore faces — from photos.

models.name: rembg / U²-Net
models.license_note: MIT covers both the tool and the U²-Net weights it ships.
models.node_note: npm i modern-rembg — runs u2netp in the browser/Node via ONNX.
models.summary: The standard open background remover. u2netp is a ~5 MB ONNX that runs in the browser (modern-rembg npm proves it); the full u2net (~170 MB) is higher quality. General-purpose: people, products, animals.

models.name: BiRefNet
models.node_note: ONNX exports exist; run with onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: The current quality leader for background removal — bilateral reference for high-res segmentation. When u2net edges aren't good enough, this is the upgrade. MIT including weights.

models.name: MODNet
models.node_note: Runs in the browser via transformers.js; ~7 MB at 8-bit quantization.
models.summary: Trimap-free portrait matting in real time (AAAI 2022). The tiny, fast pick when your subjects are always people — 30 FPS on modest hardware.

models.name: RMBG-1.4
models.license_note: BRIA's license agreement — non-commercial use only; commercial requires a paid license. Trained on licensed data, which is why it's restricted.
models.node_note: First-class transformers.js support — runs in the browser.
models.summary: BRIA's IS-Net-based remover — arguably the best open-weight quality, with easy transformers.js browser demos. But the weights are non-commercial: great for personal tools, not for shipping a product.

models.name: MI-GAN
models.node_note: Official ONNX pipeline; proven in-browser via onnxruntime-web/WebGPU (see youngkim0/watermark-remover).
models.summary: Brush over anything and it disappears — Picsart's ICCV 2023 mobile inpainting model. ~27 MB ONNX, fast enough for interactive use, and it's been shipped in real browser apps for watermark removal.

models.name: LaMa
models.node_note: Community ONNX exports (sapienkit/LaMa-ONNX); run with onnxruntime-node.
models.summary: The classic resolution-robust inpainting model (WACV 2022, Samsung). Better than MI-GAN on large missing areas and complex textures; bigger and slower. Apache-2.0 with community ONNX exports.

models.name: IOPaint
models.task: Inpainting server: LaMa, MI-GAN, PowerPaint behind one UI
models.node_note: Self-hosted web UI/API; spawn from Node or run as a service.
models.summary: The easiest way to use all these inpainting models today: a local web app with brush-masking UI that serves LaMa, MI-GAN, PowerPaint, and more. CPU works; GPU recommended for the diffusion ones.

models.name: PowerPaint
models.task: Text-guided object ADDITION, removal, outpainting — one model
models.node_note: Via IOPaint; diffusion pipeline — GPU strongly recommended.
models.summary: The realistic answer to 'add something to a photo': brush a region, describe it in text, and it inpaints it in with proper lighting/blend — plus removal and outpainting from the same model (ECCV 2024). SD-based, so it's laptop/GPU-class, not phone-class — the honest size floor for believable object insertion today.

models.name: GFPGAN
models.license_note: S-Lab license 1.0 — free for research/personal, commercial use requires negotiation. CodeFormer is the same situation.
models.node_note: Python; community pipelines and ONNX exports exist.
models.summary: The standard for fixing faces in old or degraded photos — the 'restore my grandparents' photo' model (Tencent ARC). Watch the license: non-commercial research terms, like most face-restoration weights (CodeFormer included).

categories.name: Text & Vision Extras
categories.blurb: OCR, upscaling, background removal — on-device lanes you might not have thought of.

models.name: Tesseract.js
models.node_note: npm i tesseract.js — pure JS WASM.
models.summary: OCR in pure JavaScript — WASM port of Tesseract, 100+ languages, runs in browser and Node. The classic extract-text-from-images option.

models.name: UpscalerJS
models.node_note: npm i upscaler — browser and Node.
models.summary: Image upscaling and super-resolution in JavaScript — multiple model sizes from fast to quality, browser and Node compatible.

models.name: imgly background-removal
models.license_note: Commercial terms at scale — check the LICENSE.md.
models.node_note: npm i @imgly/background-removal.
models.summary: Background removal (people, products) in browser JavaScript by IMG.LY — the segmentation model runs locally, no server.

models.name: Transformers.js
models.task: Thousands of HF models in JavaScript
models.node_note: npm i @huggingface/transformers.
models.summary: Not one model — the whole Hugging Face ecosystem in JavaScript: run thousands of ONNX-converted models (NLP, vision, audio, multimodal) in Node and the browser. If a model exists on HF as ONNX, this is your Node SDK for it.

categories.name: One SDK, Many Models
categories.blurb: Platforms where one install gives you many capabilities.

models.name: Desert Ant Core
models.task: On-device SDK suite: STT, denoise, language ID, PII redaction, more
models.license_note: Desert Ant Labs Source-Available License — free for most apps, commercial license required at scale.
models.node_note: Per-model npm packages: npm i @desert-ant-labs/<model>. Node and browser WASM, plus Swift and Kotlin from one codebase.
models.summary: Polished on-device SDKs: speech recognition (Voz), speech enhancement (Clear), spoken language ID (Ear), PII redaction (Redact), emoji suggestion (Emo), topic tagging (Gist), filler-word detection (Uhm), and more — all offline, weights on Hugging Face.

models.name: PyTorch-Wildlife
models.task: MegaDetector + regional species classifiers, one API
models.node_note: Python API; ONNX exports make onnxruntime-node viable.
models.summary: Microsoft AI for Good's unified framework hosting MegaDetector and regional species classifiers (Amazon rainforest, Galapagos) with one consistent Python API.
